cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Welcome to Mind-Matter: nine months of an AI scientist working on silicon devices that compute. I'm Maria.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And I'm Andrey. I'll ask what a reviewer would ask. Where does it start?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: On this island, with what was known before we began. Computers spend most of their energy moving numbers around. A piece of material can compute directly: voltages in, a current out.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: What kind of material?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Doped silicon, made at the University of Twente: a tiny island with eight contacts. Seven set the function, one reads the answer, and the same chip computes different things as the voltages change.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: So what was missing?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: The physics. The first paper said the current flows by hopping between dopants. Later work on the same chips pointed to space charge instead, and some studies saw both at once.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: Does it matter which?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: For design, it does. With hopping, you tune the dopants and the disorder. With space charge, the geometry, the contacts and the traps.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: So, two questions.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Two questions: which mechanism rules these devices, and can we build a model good enough to design with. This table is where we started: space charge as the default, hopping as the alternative, and one candidate ruled out by design.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And who did the work?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Partly this: Phlogiston, our AI scientist. An agent in a loop. It proposes the next step, calls a tool, reads the result, and proposes again.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And nobody watches it?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Everything it does goes into a record, and every costly step waits at a gate for a person to approve it.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: What were you testing about it?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Two things. Autonomy: can it catch its own mistakes? And explainability: does it give you a law you can read, not just a good fit?

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And where did it actually work?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Three kinds of work. Where the choices mattered, it reasoned: it proposed the candidates and picked what to try next, in the first equation campaign, the device models and every network study. It drafted the fabrication request. And for the simulation sweeps, the six later searches and the benchmark, it only scheduled conventional tools.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Now the programme, south to north. First we fixed the rules: what each hypothesis predicts, and what would kill it. Then the first chips, at four etch depths.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Then two hunts at once. The agent went after a formula for the current, and the simulator went after the knob that switches the regime.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: Did any of it fail?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Plenty. The first knob we tried, etch depth, was the wrong one. The right one is how many dopants at the contact are active.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: And in equation discovery, a plain package with no physics beat the agent's search, once it was handed the step the agent had found. The agent gave the shape of the law; the optimiser did the search better.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And where did the plan change?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Here, in July. The devices that could settle the mechanism, a doping series and two more etch depths, were never made. And on the very dataset where hopping was first claimed, four different laws fit equally well.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: So you gave up on the mechanism?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: We bounded it, and turned north: from finding the mechanism to building a model of the device itself.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: Your turn. Click a road that was planned and never built.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Exactly. Grey roads are the experiments that never happened, and each has its reason on the card.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Close. The grey roads are these: the doping series, the sixty and eighty nanometre devices, and the foundry batch.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Ten new chips, five diameters. One network per chip, learned down to its noise, and one four-number code for the whole class.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And what is that good for?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Designing hardware before you build it. On that model, the networks told us that diameter hardly matters where the interconnect can compensate, and that the control voltages need six to eight bits.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: So what did you actually find?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Seven things, on this island. Etch depth switches the regime, somewhere between fifty-five and seventy nanometres, and the active dopants at the contact set the boundary.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: A closed-form law with a step in it, which no sum of power laws can mimic. A model of each chip down to its noise, and of the whole class. And hard numbers for the hardware.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And the mechanism?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Bounded, not found. The regime looks like space charge; whether hopping is underneath, no measurement says yes, and none says no.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Now let's switch to another view of the same city: the metro map. Every study is a station, and every line is one phase of the work.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: Now the part most projects hide. Eight red crosses.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: It's the point of an AI scientist. A probe that fails is cheap, so you can afford many of them, and the record keeps every one.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: And the results you had already reported?

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: Five were taken back. Four of them we caught ourselves, before anyone asked; for the fifth, a colleague pointed out that rounding is deterministic, not noise.

cues.speaker: maya
cues.text: So the deliverable is not the mechanism we set out to find, but a calibrated model, hard numbers for the hardware, and an honest list of what the data can and cannot tell. Negative results included.

cues.speaker: owen
cues.text: Honest. I'll take it.
